topics.title: zephyr: ignore a replaced worker incarnation
topics.body:
Zephyr workers now send a random `incarnation` token with `register_worker`, `pull_task`, and `heartbeat`. The coordinator tracks the current incarnation for each `worker_id`. A `pull_task` from a replaced incarnation returns `SHUTDOWN`, so the old attempt exits without taking a shard; its `heartbeat` no longer refreshes liveness.

Iris can start a new attempt of a lost worker task while the old one is still running, with both attempts using the same `worker_id`. The old attempt could pull a shard after the new one registered and then die. Heartbeats from the new attempt kept the `worker_id` alive, leaving that shard in flight indefinitely.[^1]

Handling of results and errors from a replaced incarnation is unchanged: re-registration already requeues its shards, and the attempt check drops stale reports. `test_replaced_incarnation_cannot_take_or_hold_a_shard` covers the failure; other test call sites pass `incarnation="i0"`.

[^1]: This occurred three times in the datakit ferry runs (tier 1 and tier 2) on 2026-10-04, each after a preemptible v5e host was lost. Preempting the idle new attempt was the only way to continue.

Fixes #9740

topics.title: [zephyr] Shard stays in flight after Iris replaces a lost worker attempt
topics.body:
A Zephyr stage can wait forever for one shard after Iris replaces a lost worker attempt. The coordinator records the shard as in flight on a worker that never runs it, so the pipeline hangs until its job times out.

It happened three times on 2026-10-04 in the datakit ferry runs: once in the tier 1 embed pool, once in the tier 2 embed pool, and once in the tier 2 shared pool (3 shards). Each time a preemptible v5e host was lost.

Reproduce:
1. Run a Zephyr pipeline on preemptible hosts until Iris marks a worker task `worker_lost_spec` while the old attempt still runs.
2. Iris starts attempt 1 with the same worker ID (`<group>-<index>`). It registers, and the coordinator requeues the shards of that ID.
3. Attempt 0 then pulls a new shard under the same ID and dies.
4. Attempt 1 sends heartbeats for the ID, so `check_heartbeats` never fails it, and the shard stays in `in_flight`. Attempt 1 itself is idle in `_poll_loop`.

Expected: calls from a replaced attempt cannot take a shard or keep the worker ID alive, and the shard is requeued.

Evidence: the coordinator logged `105/106 complete, 1 in-flight, 1/1 workers alive` for more than 25 minutes, and a thread dump of attempt 1 showed only the poll and heartbeat threads. Preempting attempt 1 made it register again, which requeued the shard, and the run finished.

topics.title: Share Hero and Snowball checkpoint export mechanics
topics.body:
Share HF shard writing between Hero and the Levanter converter used by Snowball. A private writer owns host memory reservations, uploads and optional resume receipts. Callers keep model conversion, shard layout and destination policy.

Call from all JAX ranks with identical shard/key order and matching shapes/dtypes. Only process zero writes. Resume verifies identity and checksums before reuse. Writer failures propagate when a main thread observes them.

CPU tests cover exact output parity, BF16 shapes, budget limits, two-rank failure/recovery and Snowball overwrites. Formatting and types pass. Full-size accelerator and live cloud/HF uploads remain untested.

topics.title: Experiment: Blackwell source-push W13 inbox kernel
topics.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This experiment investigated a Blackwell MoE source-push path for the target shape `T/rank=65536`, `D=3072`, `I=3072`, total experts `256`, topk `4`. The intended true fused Warpgroup peer-reference design was ruled out because the tested JAX/Mosaic stack cannot lower peer-id GMEM refs, so the practical path became staged source-push transport plus local Blackwell compute. Transport tuning reached `1596.34` useful W13-equivalent TFLOP/s/rank on B300 with zero drops, clearing the corrected topk-expanded 60% gates. The public `moe_mlp` path now has a reusable preplanned boundary that cuts target forward steady-state from about `39.965 s` direct to `0.093318 s`, while package-private prepared runs remain faster. Backward initially OOMed at target D/I due to per-route row materialization, but regrouping by destination-local expert with a 512-row tile unblocked the full target fwd+bwd run at `1.90717 s` steady-state with zero dropped routes. The remaining recommendation is to treat staged Blackwell as the viable path and reserve further work for production API boundary decisions and a tuned Pallas backward.

### Helpful links
- Peer-ref lowering gate: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6933#issuecomment-4881270376
- Public preplanned target timing: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6933#issuecomment-4883691661
- Full target fwd+bwd unblocked: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6933#issuecomment-4884581545
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Description

Investigate a Blackwell implementation of the source-push fused all2all(lhs) + W13/GMM path for MoE. The first decision point was whether remote peer GMEM references can be used under Pallas GPU Warpgroup lowering on Blackwell. That path is unsupported on the tested JAX stack, so the active implementation direction is staged: source-push copy/pack followed by local Blackwell ragged/GMM W13 or materialized W13/SwiGLU.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Reach at least 60% of the best measured local Blackwell W13/SwiGLU throughput for the inbox-send source-push path on the target MoE shape: roughly 65K tokens, hidden_dim=3072, intermediate_dim=3072, total experts=256, topk=4. Because topk=4 expands W13 work, the apples-to-apples local compute baseline uses `M=262144` useful W13 rows per rank.

## TL;DR

The practical Blackwell path is staged, not true fused Warpgroup peer-ref. The peer-ref probe failed with `GMEM refs with peer ids are not supported in warpgroup lowering`. Corrected topk-expanded B300 local baselines are `1824.22` useful TFLOP/s/rank for W13-only and `1534.20` useful W13 TFLOP/s/rank for materialized W13/SwiGLU at `M=262144`. After copy tuning, B300 EP=8 staged transport repeat medians reached `1596.34` useful W13-equivalent TFLOP/s/rank and `267.73 GB/s/rank` with zero drops. That clears 60% of both corrected baselines: W13-only target `1094.53`, materialized W13/SwiGLU target `920.52`. A direct hand-adapted fused W13/SwiGLU epilogue remains blocked by a Mosaic `copy_gmem_to_smem` swizzle assertion even on tiny non-collective smokes.

## Results

- Peer-ref Warpgroup probe: failed at the intended decision gate with peer-id GMEM refs unsupported in Warpgroup lowering.
- Local Blackwell W13/GMM at `M=65536`: best `1.565 ms`, `1580.53` useful TFLOP/s/rank.
- Local materialized W13/SwiGLU at `M=65536`: best `1.746 ms`, `1416.95` useful W13 TFLOP/s/rank.
- Corrected topk-expanded local W13/GMM at `M=262144`: `5.425 ms`, `1824.22` useful TFLOP/s/rank.
- Corrected topk-expanded local materialized W13/SwiGLU at `M=262144`: `6.450 ms`, `1534.20` useful W13 TFLOP/s/rank.
- Initial B300 EP=8 target source-push transport repeat medians: `copy_release_only` median `10.284 ms`, `161.39 GB/s/rank`, `962.26` useful W13-equivalent TFLOP/s/rank, zero route/row/entry drops.
- Tuned B300 EP=8 target source-push transport repeat medians with `inbox_slots=24`, `send_worker_programs_per_peer=4`: `6.199 ms`, `267.73 GB/s/rank`, `1596.34` useful W13-equivalent TFLOP/s/rank, zero route/row/entry drops.
- Fused W13/SwiGLU prototype: not lowering. Reducing pipeline depth avoids one shared-memory limit, but the prototype still hits `assert copy_params.get("swizzle") is None` in Mosaic copy lowering.

## Scope

- Add a Blackwell-only implementation path without rewriting the existing Hopper source-push kernel.
- Keep Hopper and Blackwell benchmark rows separate in JSONL artifacts.
- Compare local Blackwell GMM/W13, W13/SwiGLU, copy-only, and inbox-send staged/fused variants.
- Prefer the staged Blackwell path until Warpgroup peer refs or the fused epilogue lowering issue changes upstream.

## Decision log

- 2026-07-04: Start with peer-ref capability probe before tuning fused source-push W13.
- 2026-07-04: Peer-id GMEM refs are unsupported in Warpgroup lowering on the tested stack; switch to staged copy/pack plus local Blackwell compute.
- 2026-07-04: Use tuned local W13 config `128x128x64`, `max_concurrent_steps=6`, `collective=True`, `grid_minor_dim=M`, `epilogue_tile_n=64`.
- 2026-07-04: Corrected B300 topk-expanded local baselines use `M=262144`.
- 2026-07-04: B300 staged transport with `inbox_slots=24`, `send_worker_programs_per_peer=4` clears 60% of both corrected W13-only and materialized W13/SwiGLU baselines.
- 2026-07-04: Direct hand-adapted fused W13/SwiGLU remains a lowering follow-up, not the current practical path.

## Negative results index

- Warpgroup peer-id GMEM refs: unsupported in lowering on the tested stack.
- Upstream local W13 sweep: most `collective=False` rows failed from an unbound cluster-axis path; larger memory/layout configs failed from shared-memory or layout constraints.
- Direct fused W13/SwiGLU epilogue: still blocked by Mosaic copy lowering assertion after small-shape, non-collective, lower-pipeline-depth, and single-contiguous-W13-SMEM isolation attempts.
- Earlier `M=65536` local baseline comparison was not apples-to-apples with the EP=8 `topk=4` source-push transport row; corrected local compute baselines use `M=262144`.

## Current baseline

- Existing Hopper source-plan W13 context from `.agents/logbooks/6597-moe-mgpu-forward.md`: `8.441 ms`, `215.94` rounded TFLOP/s/rank, `203.54` useful TFLOP/s/rank on that Hopper target shape.
- Blackwell local W13 baseline at `M=262144`: `1824.22` useful TFLOP/s/rank.
- Blackwell materialized W13/SwiGLU baseline at `M=262144`: `1534.20` useful W13 TFLOP/s/rank.
- 60% targets: `1094.53` useful TFLOP/s/rank against W13-only; `920.52` against materialized W13/SwiGLU.
- Tuned B300 staged transport repeat median: `1596.34` useful W13-equivalent TFLOP/s/rank.

## Links

- Research logbook: `.agents/logbooks/blackwell-source-push-inbox.md`
- Related Hopper/source-push context: `.agents/logbooks/6597-moe-mgpu-forward.md`
- JAX reference kernel: https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/blob/main/jax/experimental/pallas/ops/gpu/blackwell_ragged_dot_mgpu.py

topics.title: [iris] Quarantine nodes with persistent isolated S3 failures
topics.body:
Add opt-in regional S3 read/write/delete probes to the Kubernetes node-agent so a node that remains Ready while storage requests stall can be quarantined before it receives more work. The probe uses the task storage environment, a tiny object per node incarnation, and a process deadline that bounds SDK retries and DNS stalls.

The controller cordons persistent failures only when a fresh majority of nodes successfully probed the same target after the failure began. A persistent cordon budget defaults to one node, and credential/configuration errors reset the failure streak. Node UID, boot ID, report freshness, and Kubernetes resource versions fence stale observations and concurrent operator changes.

Health and cordon evidence remain in node annotations even when Finelog is unavailable. Recovery requires an operator to uncordon the repaired node and release its budget annotation; running tasks are not evicted. Configuration, scratch-object lifecycle requirements, and recovery are documented in the CoreWeave guide.

Context: [node-local storage failure during the hero run](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/599).

topics.title: Pod creation fails on a node with 65K empty Silo cgroups
topics.body:
On October 2, new pods failed to start on CoreWeave node `g5bc6da`, blocking new jobs. Kubernetes reported `no space left on device` while creating a pod’s cgroup, the kernel group used to track and limit container resources. The node still reported healthy, and its filesystem had 3.55 TB free.

The host cgroup tree had 65,535 descendant groups. Of these, 65,412 were under `/silo`; that entire subtree contained no processes. This strongly suggests exhaustion of the kernel’s roughly 64K memory-cgroup ID space, though we have not traced the failing allocator.

Silo is the nested container runtime running inside our privileged Iris job `muchanem.cap-pipeline-host-53`. Two sampled container IDs from its `containerd-shim` processes matched empty `/silo` cgroups. This points to a cleanup problem in that workload’s runtime, but we have not identified the code path responsible. We have no evidence that CoreWeave’s host containerd created these groups.

Please investigate whether completed containers leave cgroups and shim processes behind, and fix the cleanup path. Verify that repeated container creation and teardown do not keep increasing either count. Coordinate cleanup of the affected node with the pipeline owner; an empty cgroup alone does not establish that it is safe to remove while the runtime is active.

comments.body:
🤖 Silo's sandbox deletion leaked every gVisor (`runsc`) sandbox. All Silo hosts are now stopped and their leaked cgroups removed. Silo stays down until a host with the fix is deployed.

**Cause**

Silo deletes a sandbox with `nerdctl rm -f`. Under `runsc`, nerdctl 2.1.2 kills the sandbox and then tries to delete the task. The delete kills again, `runsc kill` fails with "sandbox is not running", and nerdctl exits 0 anyway. The stopped task, its `containerd-shim`, and its `/silo/<id>` cgroup stay. Silo saw exit 0 and counted the sandbox as deleted.

Reproduced on `cap-pipeline-host-53` (2026-10-04): the same `nerdctl run` then `rm -f` removes everything with `runc`. With `runsc` it exits 0, and the container, its `STOPPED` task, its shim and its empty cgroup remain. The leaked containers carried the label `nerdctl/error: unknown error after kill: runsc did not terminate successfully: exit status 128: sandbox is not running`. Host-53's nested containerd held 19,415 such containers.

**Fix**

`NerdctlRuntime.remove` now checks containerd after `nerdctl rm -f`. If the container is still there, it runs `ctr task delete` (no kill, since the task is already stopped) and then `ctr container delete`. About 0.2% of leaked containers also had `runsc` state that still said "running" for a dead sandbox, and their task delete was refused. For those, `remove` runs `runsc delete --force` first. If the container still cannot be deleted, `remove` raises: the sandbox stays `destroying` and the host's reaper retries it. On host-53, both steps removed the shim and the cgroup. A regression test covers both cases. The fix is on the `mark/silo` branch and is not yet pushed.

**Cleanup (owner-run, 2026-10-04 ~23:05–23:45 UTC)**

All hosts were idle (0 running sandboxes) during the cleanup.

1. On each of the 17 `cap-pipeline-host-*` pods on cw-us-east-02a, I deleted every container with a `STOPPED` task through that host's own containerd, using the sequence above. Live sandbox tasks are `RUNNING`, so they were not touched.
2. I then removed `/silo/<id>` cgroups that were empty, older than 30 minutes, and unknown to that host's containerd.

The node-wide memory `num_cgroups` count fell from 10K–35K to 700–1,250 on 15 nodes. I then cancelled all 17 hosts. The 3 `cap-rno` hosts on cw-rno2a had no leaked containers in their containerd; the sweep removed 10,481 orphaned cgroups on one node and 510 on the other, and those hosts are cancelled too. The `cap-pipeline` broker is still running; it creates no cgroups.

**Not resolved**

- I could not finish two cw-us-east-02a nodes before cancelling. Their empty `/silo` cgroups remain until the cleanup script runs or the node reboots:
  - the node of `cap-pipeline-host-52`, about 33K at the start, where exec stopped responding;
  - the node of `cap-pipeline-host-47`, about 4.3K, where the cleanup was still running.
- About 1–2 containers per host had a zombie sandbox process, and `runsc delete --force` hangs on them. Cancelling the pod clears them. With the fix, `remove` times out after 300 s, logs the failure, and retries on the next reap.
- The cw-rno2a node of `cap-rno-host-4`/`-9` still reports about 12K memory cgroups, but 11,958 of them are dying cgroups (deleted, still pinned by page cache). The kernel frees these as the cache is reclaimed.
- Repeated create and teardown on a deployed host with the fix has not been run yet. It will be checked on the first host brought back, by watching memory `num_cgroups` and the shim count.

topics.title: Add GB200 launcher and H100 pipeline validation
topics.body:
Add a GB200 pipeline launcher and a bounded H100 validation runner for the model recipe from main `89ac0d770506f7e27ca217760ec5ca3246694e7e`. The launcher uses FP32 parameters, BF16 compute, compute-scaled MuonH, SM100 ragged transport and Flash Attention. It requests one hard NVLink domain in the opportunistic BATCH queue and separates queue wait from worker execution deadlines. Future run names use `pipeline-gb200-*` or `pipeline-h100-*`.

Executable `0da04acccf7b0842319a8668d71ccc697a7b10ec` completed the corrected eight-GB200 gate with two full-width layers, PP2/EP4 and sequence length 4096. The two losses were 11.806337356567383 and 0.4912489652633667. All eight native GPU processes, both Iris GPU tasks and the coordinator exited zero. All 48 startup task ABI records had zero input memory-kind mismatches. Both coordinator failure and preemption retry caps were zero; the SDK launch example sets both explicitly because the CLI retry option controls failure retries only. [GB200 setup and standalone commands](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/hero-gb200-pipeline/experiments/grug/moe_hero_pipeline/GB200.md) record prerequisites and acceptance criteria.

The combined H100 runner was validated at `a1e3ab278eeb05bb645db641dd3e7dabedf90dbb` on 16 H100s with two full-width layers, PP2/EP8 and sequence length 4096. Ten synthetic updates had finite losses from 11.804966926574707 to 0.4793720245361328. Twenty fresh Harrier updates consumed 2,621,440 tokens with finite losses from 11.8075590133667 to 7.612007141113281. All 200 raw components remained nonempty with their original mixture weights and order. Both GPU tasks and supervisors exited zero; fresh-data logs retain 15 individual rank exits, while the supervisor's child-reaping contract certifies all 16. No checkpoint was written. These runs used the explicit SM90 pooled-wave/FA4 adapter with SYRK disabled and establish no H100 ragged-transport parity. [H100 reference](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/hero-gb200-pipeline/docs/references/hero-pipeline-h100.md) separates these runs from the historical reduced-model checkpoint comparison.

The runtime pins upstream JAXPP `328f75a80cecf22c7cc030a82d8941d3c1e220b6` plus a tracked host-memory/startup overlay. JAX 0.11.1 overrides JAXPP's declared compatibility cap and remains experimental; CUDA dependencies with lower bounds are recorded per launch. Installer recovery avoids duplicate global reinstall flags, including on deployed older worker wrappers. The [Iris installer incident record](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/600) distinguishes the initiating GitHub fetch failure from the broken recovery command. Main-recipe argument parsing rejects AdamW before distributed initialization. Shared pipeline configuration, process ownership, array predicates, data scheduling and loader cleanup consolidate the overlapping work from #9279 and #9460.

Required lint, type checks, hooks and strict docs checks passed. The affected safe suite passed 5,562 tests with 18 skips and six expected failures. The lint-catalog review completed; findings were fixed or answered. Before merge, the positional compiled-initialization triple must be replaced with a named result and the runner lifecycle split further. Those deferred structural changes need separate transport and lifecycle validation.

Full 48-layer main-recipe execution remains unvalidated. The 64-GB200 rack attempt acquired its allocation and started some native processes, then failed during runtime installation; it produced no finite training updates. The full 192-H100/48-layer/65K run remains held. This pull request remains draft.

topics.title: Experiment: Grug MoE d2560 H100 MFU
topics.body:
## Description

Track the work to make the issue #6044 d=2560 May Recipe Grug MoE shape fast on CoreWeave H100s. The target is a repeatable profile-bearing short run at >=20% training MFU, followed by profile-evidence optimization of MoE, attention, FSDP/sharding, cross entropy, data/host overhead, and optimizer/update overhead.

## Hypothesis or Goal

The current Grug MoE path can reach >=20% MFU for the d=2560, 26-layer, 256-expert, top-k 4 shape if the H100 topology is kept to a viable expert-parallel layout and the remaining hot paths are optimized from measured profiles rather than guessed.

### Links

* Source recipe: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6044#issuecomment-4607416665
* Research logbook: `.agents/logbooks/grug-moe-d2560-mfu.md`
* Branch logbook: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/codex/research-grug-moe-d2560-mfu/.agents/logbooks/grug-moe-d2560-mfu.md
* Latest checkpoint: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/55847db99
* Latest run: `/dlwh/iris-run-job-20260615-065544` (`GM2560-MAY-036B64-N8-FASTPROFILE-cw-20260615-0655`)
* Latest W&B: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/GM2560-MAY-036B64-N8-FASTPROFILE-cw-20260615-0655

<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## TL;DR

No >=20 MFU claim yet. The current live run is `GM2560-MAY-036B64-N8-FASTPROFILE-cw-20260615-0655`, parent `/dlwh/iris-run-job-20260615-065544`, on `cw-us-east-02a`. It follows the updated direction to reduce batch size rather than add train-time microbatching: full d2560/L26, seq_len 4096, batch 64, N8/EP8/model1, ring MoE, FA4/CuTe attention, XLA CE, replicated embeddings, `compute_with_master`, `save_moe`, W&B tracker, and the earliest callback-eligible profiler window (`profiler_start=3`, `profiler_steps=1`, HLO proto enabled). MAY-034 hit a pre-step 128-device clique stall; MAY-035 B128/N8 stayed pre-first-step without metrics in a short window, so MAY-036 reduces global batch to 64 while keeping the 64-GPU launch size.

The memory evidence localizes the original B256 blocker to full-depth, sequence/batch-scaled activation or workspace pressure. Full-depth B256 failed before the first step across fp32 live params, bf16 live params with fp32 master, Pallas CE, and `recompute_all`; full-depth B128 succeeded; one-layer B256 succeeded; full-depth B256 at seq2048 succeeded. MAY-032 at seq3072 was killed before first-step evidence, so it is not evidence for or against that memory bracket.
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Scope

Baseline shape from #6044: d=2560, 26 layers, 20 Q heads, 5 KV heads, head_dim 128, 256 experts, top-k 4, seq_len 4096, half-RoPE, PKO on every 4th plus last layer, routing renorm sum 2.5, router z-loss 0, ring MoE, MuonH, mixed precision `params=float32,compute=bfloat16,output=bfloat16`.

## Current Baseline

Current executable profile target: 8 H100 nodes, `MAY_EXPERT_AXIS=8`, `MAY_MODEL_AXIS=1`, `MAY_REPLICA_AXIS=1`, `MAY_BATCH=64`, `MAY_SEQ_LEN=4096`, `MAY_STEPS=4`, `MAY_DATA=synthetic`, `MAY_TRACKER=wandb`, `MAY_CHECKPOINTS=none`, `MAY_PROFILER_START=3`, `MAY_PROFILER_STEPS=1`, `MAY_PROFILER_ENABLE_HLO_PROTO=true`, `MAY_WATCH_INTERVAL=0`, `MAY_ATTENTION_IMPLEMENTATION=gpu_fa4_cute`, `MAY_CE_IMPLEMENTATION=xla`, `MAY_LIVE_PARAM_MODE=compute_with_master`, `MAY_INPUT_EMBED_SHARDING=replicated`, `MAY_OUTPUT_PROJ_SHARDING=replicated`, and `MAY_REMAT=save_moe`.

Original full-B256 target gate remains memory-negative at seq4096. Latest successful B256 diagnostic: same as the target gate except `MAY_SEQ_LEN=2048` in `GM2560-MAY-031S2048-B256-N16-cw-20260615-0520`.

## Results

No >=20 MFU claim yet. Search space reduced so far:

* Replicating input/output embeddings removed the old `%fake_parameter.2 = bf16[1,4096,2560]` full-rematerialization warning on the one-layer layout probe.
* FA4/CuTe backward now compiles with the CUTLASS atomic wrapper.
* Full-depth B256 on N16/EP8/model1 still OOMed before the first step at ~74 GiB under three one-axis variants: fp32 live params, bf16 live params with fp32 master, and Pallas CE.
* Full-depth B128 fits, and one-layer B256 fits. This localizes the current B256 blocker to full-depth activation/remat liveness rather than static optimizer/parameter storage or the loss/output local-token workspace alone.
* Full-depth B256 with `recompute_all` still OOMs before the first step, but the request drops to 72.03 GiB. That makes sequence/token scaling the next diagnostic axis rather than another param/optimizer-state probe.
* Full-depth B256 with `seq_len=2048` and `recompute_all` succeeds on N16/EP8/model1. The run produced no usable MFU row, but it proves the remaining memory blocker is sequence/token-scaled.
* MAY-032 (`seq_len=3072`, B256) was killed before a first-step metric or allocator result, so it is not memory evidence.
* MAY-033 was healthy but intentionally stopped before first metrics/profile because `profiler_start=6` would delay evidence on the slow B128 path.
* MAY-034 hit a pre-step `Initialize clique: devices=128` rendezvous stall with zero W&B history/profile and was intentionally stopped.
* MAY-035 B128/N8 was intentionally stopped pre-first-step after a short no-progress window with zero W&B scalar history.
* MAY-036 is live as the reduced-batch B64 N8 fast-profile/MFU run, with W&B and the earliest callback-eligible profiler window enabled.

## Decision Log

* 2026-06-13: Use fp32 sharded params plus bf16 compute for the baseline. `params=bfloat16` remains a diagnostic knob, not the requested fp32-master mode.
* 2026-06-14: Force XLA cross entropy after Pallas CE caused autotune noise and a full-logits-shaped startup allocation.
* 2026-06-14: Treat mixed default ring EP plus `model_axis>1` as invalid for now after repeated local `kCollectivePermute`/rendezvous failures.
* 2026-06-14: Keep production MoE topology at `expert_axis=8`, `model_axis=1`, `moe_implementation=ring` until a non-ring backend proves otherwise.
* 2026-06-14: Disable checkpoints, profiler, watch stats, and W&B for executable-gate runs; only relaunch with profiler once the shape can step.
* 2026-06-15: Use replicated input/output embeddings for the full May gates because the one-layer layout probe removed the old SPMD full-remat warning.
* 2026-06-15: Treat full-depth B256 memory as activation/remat-liveness dominated after B128 full-depth and one-layer B256 both fit.
* 2026-06-15: Use sequence length as the next one-axis diagnostic after `recompute_all` only reduced the B256 full-depth request to 72.03 GiB.
* 2026-06-15: Since full-depth B256 `seq_len=2048` fits, recover full sequence length by attacking token/activation pressure before launching the profile-bearing full-shape run.
* 2026-06-15: Per updated direction, reduce global batch to B128 instead of adding train-time microbatch accumulation, and use the fitting full-sequence shape for the first profile-bearing MFU run.
* 2026-06-15: Replace MAY-033 with MAY-034 using `profiler_start=3`, `profiler_steps=1`, and HLO proto enabled so the first profile artifact arrives as soon as callback gating permits.
* 2026-06-15: Stop MAY-034 after persistent pre-step 128-device clique rendezvous warnings; relaunch as MAY-035 on 8 nodes / 64 H100s to get profile evidence while isolating N16 launch stability.
* 2026-06-15: Stop MAY-035 after it stayed pre-first-step with no W&B rows in a short evidence window; relaunch as MAY-036 with global batch 64 rather than adding microbatching.

## Negative Results Index

* GM2560-MFU-004/005: failed before step 0 with allocator requests around 60 GiB; no W&B history or profile artifact.
* GM2560-MFU-006: moved past the old allocator signal with 0.95 XLA memory fraction, then wedged pre-metrics in XLA collective/clique startup; no W&B scalar history or profile artifact.
* GM2560-MFU-007 and GM2560-MAY-020: reproduced the 256-device clique/JAX coordination fatal path around the old `%fake_parameter.2` activation-layout warning.
* GM2560-MIN-009/011/012: mixed ring EP plus model-axis sharding failed before metrics with collective/rendezvous symptoms. This is a topology/backend negative result, not evidence against EP8/model1.
* GM2560-MAY-025: full-depth B256 with fp32 live params failed before step 0 with `74.75GiB` allocation request.
* GM2560-MAY-026: same shape with bf16 live params plus fp32 master failed before step 0 with `74.42GiB` allocation request.
* GM2560-MAY-027: same shape with Pallas CE failed before step 0 with `74.41GiB` allocation request.
* GM2560-MAY-030: same full-depth B256 shape with `recompute_all` failed before step 0 with `72.03GiB` allocation request.

## Conclusion

Open. The original full d2560 B256 shape remains memory-negative at seq4096; the current path is to finish the profile-bearing B64 full-sequence run, then use the profile to decide whether attention, MoE EP communication, FSDP/update, or optimizer work is the next bottleneck.

topics.title: [grug] Raise hero single-rack MFU from 28.2% to 31.1%
topics.body:
On one GB200 NVL72 rack, these commits shorten the `moe_hero_ep` training step from 13.90 to 12.61 s (28.24% to 31.13% MFU), with loss inside the run-to-run noise of unchanged code. The last commit adds a PGLE profile builder; with a profile built from the program's own trace, the step is 12.52 s (31.37% MFU). The changes come from two campaigns: the first worked down the step's most expensive scopes, and the second benchmarked OLMo-core 3's BF16 MoE kernels against this path (#9636) and kept the leads that paid.

Each row is one single-rack run (`cw-us-east-08a`, 64 GPUs) restored from `hero-fa4sm100-nomask-step146k` step 180000, seed 0, 100 steps, on main's production PJRT wheel with the code's defaults. The time is the median step duration over steps 180011-180099 without the three profiled steps, and the gain is the previous row's time divided by this row's, minus one. Repeated runs of the same code differ by about 0.1%. The runs used trees from before a final round of refactors and review fixes (types, helpers, comments, tests, and code paths the hero does not take); the hero's train step lowers to the same program at these commits.

| Change | Commit | s/step | MFU | Gain |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| main | b4d1761ff2 | 13.899 | 28.24% | |
| Remat discounts the host-offloaded carry | 13448300c6 | 13.737 | 28.57% | +1.18% |
| Unfilled ragged transport buffers | a544f2571c | 13.542 | 28.99% | +1.44% |
| Expert-side routing-weight gradient | 9ea5098c10 | 13.130 | 29.90% | +3.14% |
| Streaming Triton short convolution | 98412f4efc | 13.059 | 30.06% | +0.55% |
| SwiGLU backward in the dh GEMM epilogue | 50e50512a5 | 12.943 | 30.33% | +0.89% |
| Device-side kernel availability check | 1f08c52720 | | | no hero change |
| Triton router top-k | 42fc5766b3 | 12.875 | 30.49% | +0.53% |
| Token-major dispatch scatter | 0ba2cb6bbd | 12.730 | 30.83% | +1.14% |
| Shared and chunk GEMMs under the MoE transports | 45c2459f70 | 12.638 | 31.06% | +0.73% |
| Synchronous collectives without the carry offload | 8fd3af2759 | | | no hero change |
| Shared-expert SwiGLU in QuACK epilogues | ffecc63a46 | 12.652 | 31.03% | -0.11% |
| No routed pre-activation store under remat | 9ce3cfc1a4 | 12.611 | 31.13% | +0.33% |
| PGLE profile builder, run with a profile | daa46e2be5 | 12.515 | 31.37% | +0.77% |

The scheduling row groups three changes that do not stand alone. The MLP-section weight prefetch (from #9481) lets the first shared expert's gate/up projection run beside the first ragged dispatch, but it also moves a weight slice behind each layer's carry offload copy on the same memcpy stream, which stalls the forward for 98-152 ms/step on the production wheel. The barrier that issues the slices before the carry copy removes that stall, and costs 0.49% on a program that does not collide; at the end of the series, disabling it alone slows the step by 0.79%. The shared-expert QuACK row is negative because, after the scheduling row, the shared GEMMs are what covers the transports: the 0.18 s/step of compute it saves left 0.24 s/step more transport exposed. Removing it from the end of the series still slows the step, by 0.35% and 0.22% in two pairs, so it stays.

Changes whose gain was below about 0.3% were removed from the final tip one at a time and kept only if the tip slowed by more than 0.2% without them; a result between 0.2% and 0.4% got a second pair. That dropped a scatter-based inverse permutation (the tip was 0.04% faster without it) and a Triton bincount (0.22% and 0.10%), and kept the routed pre-activation change (0.47%) and the shared-expert QuACK change. The four rows from the unfilled transport buffers through the dh-epilogue SwiGLU backward were measured with the inverse permutation in their base and before a behavior-neutral review cleanup; without it, the last of them ran the same 12.943 s.

Numerics: the unfilled transport buffers, the top-k kernel, the dispatch scatter and the pre-activation change are bitwise. The routing-weight gradient, the dh-epilogue SwiGLU backward and the short convolution's weight gradient change at bf16 rounding; the shared-expert SwiGLU now runs on the fp32 accumulator, so the forward changes at rounding level and 0.06-0.3% of routing assignments differ downstream, as close to an fp32 reference as before; the carry barrier moves fusion boundaries. On the ragged backend, an accepted assignment whose combine weight is zero, or small enough for `w * dout` to underflow, gets a zero combine-weight gradient rather than `<dout, y>`, which `moe_mlp` documents; sigmoid and softmax routers produce such weights only by underflow, where their logit gradient is as small. Against main over 100 steps, the final tip's loss differs by at most 3.8e-4 (2.6e-4 with the profile), against 3.3e-4 between two runs of main. Four of about 30 runs took a late upward excursion of about 1e-3 that value-identical variants also showed, so it is run-to-run nondeterminism.

Peak HBM rises from 103.1 to 123.2 GiB of a 143.75 GiB pool, mainly the 18 GiB routed MoE output that the expert-side routing-weight gradient saves; under the carry offload the launcher defaults to `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.78` and slop 105, validated on one rack only. A ragged run without the carry offload keeps XLA's default scheduler, which ignores the one-in-flight collective limit, so that configuration now runs collectives synchronously; the hero always offloads and is unaffected. PGLE needs a profile built from a trace of the exact program and mesh, so the production run needs its own before it gains the last row; automatic PGLE stays off. The memcpy-stream collision is avoided per program here; the patched PJRT wheel that gives host transfers their own streams is left for a follow-up.

This supersedes #9481: it carries that PR's mirror transpose parameters, weight prefetch and PGLE builder, and replaces its two-stage chunk pipelining with the dispatch overlap above, which with PGLE measured 12.666 s/step against 12.783 for pipelining with PGLE, the latter on a patched PJRT wheel without the copy stall (both before the kernels above and the shared-expert change). Part of #9636; the OLMo-core comparison and its adopt/defer/reject table are on that issue. Research records: `.agents/logbooks/mfu30.md` and `.agents/logbooks/olmo9636.md` on `research/mcwitt/mfu30`.

topics.title: [datakit] Register the hero quality data as Datakit steps
topics.body:
Register the hero quality data as two Datakit steps and make the store-ready
dataset a StepSpec output. `bucket.quality_step` reads three co-partitioned leaves
of a source (the normalized shard for row order, the fusion score leaf, and the
content-type leaf), applies the per-type calibration, and writes one shard per
basename with `source`, `id`, `content_type`, `raw_score`, `score` and
`quality_bucket` in the normalized row order. Its artifact is the `QualityScores`
the store already consumes, so `build_clustered_store` reads it unchanged.
`hero_data.quality` resolves that step's identity, and `run.py --stage bucket`
produces it for every registered source.

`score_fusion.fusion_score_step` is the producer of record for the raw scores: one
Zephyr task per normalized shard on GPU workers, tokenizing the text through the
tokenize stage's own core and reading the Harrier embedding by position. The Nemotron
tokenize leaves the August 14 run read were deleted from S3 after it, so the run's
scores are registered by path map as `hero_data.fusion_scores` rather than
rescored; a rerun of the score stage lands at the step's own identity. The
content-type leaves written beside those scores are registered the same way as
`hero_data.content_type`, and `hero_data.harrier` now returns a frozen step so the
score step can depend on it.

Every input leaf of a source holds the normalized shard's documents in its row
order. A census over all 162,535 shards of the 292 sources found every
fusion-score, content-type and Harrier shard in exactly the normalized order, with
the same ids and row counts. Both steps therefore read their side inputs by
position and check each batch's ids against the normalized shard, so a leaf from a
different normalize run fails its shard. `QualityScores.samples_output_dir` is
removed; the stage report reads its spot-check text from the normalized shard of
the same basename.

The model directory moves to `datakit/models/quality/nemotron_88k`, relative to
`MARIN_PREFIX`, with the config fields of the removed bigram, MoE, frozen-donor
and dtype arms dropped from `model.py` and the saved meta. `QualityPin` carries
separate digests for the scorer artifacts and the calibration file, checked by the
worker before it writes, so a refit calibration moves the bucketed dataset without
moving or rescoring the raw scores. Manifest entries for `harrier`, `fusion_scores`,
`content_type` and `quality` cover all 292 sources. The fusion checkpoint's
document-embedding weights form one optional `DocFusion` submodule whose field
order matches the serialized leaves, so the deployed checkpoint loads to identical
weights and scores, and the calibration file parses into a `Calibration`
dataclass.

The bucket stage has run over all 292 sources: 18,710,478,349 documents in
162,535 shards, equal to the fusion-score totals, in 2h50m with 12 sources in
flight on CPU workers. On `nsf_awards` (3 shards, 381,789 documents) the output
reproduced the normalized row order, the pinned raw scores and content types, and
the calibrated buckets on every row. The score stage run from text against the
same embeddings matched the pinned scores to a maximum difference of 1.6e-3 (mean
2.3e-4), the bf16 reduction-order noise of a 4,096-document batch against the
earlier 32,768.

topics.title: [fast-track] Marin Belay v1: hill-climb the scaling ladder (Paloma macro loss, 8 min on 8×H100)
topics.body:
This issue tracks iterative improvements to the Marin pretraining scaling ladder (`experiments/grug/fast_track`) using the **Marin Belay** process. It is a twist on autoresearch: an agent runs experiments in batches, and anyone can steer it with research directions. > **To suggest a research direction, comment on [Marin Belay Intake (#9514)](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9514).** Suggestions a maintainer approves (👍 from a `marin-devs` member) are copied into this thread automatically, and the agent acts only on this thread. This thread holds the agent's batch reports and maintainer steering. ![fast_track MoE ladder: Marin 535B baseline, clean KMA and candidate 9](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/9697c11ef215ec0f9d536a1bceb0876f768fcf26/v1/ladder_scaling.png) The Marin 535B compute-optimal baseline follows `L(C) = 1.2 + 59.0·C^(−0.0843)` over four data-matched rungs. Clean KMA, the current baseline (★), is 0.022 lower at d512, 0.049 lower at d768, 0.040 lower at d1024 and 0.033 lower at d1280, which is about 1.14×, 1.43×, 1.40× and 1.35× the baseline's compute efficiency. Its dashed curve is fit to all four points: `L(C) = 1.2 + 64.8·C^(−0.0870)`. The **?** marks the open question this issue is chasing: how much further down each point can go. The red diamonds are the current best recipe, candidate 9 (Status below): **2.977 / 2.725 / 2.515 / 2.397** at d512 / d768 / d1024 / d1280. d512 and d768 are seed means, and the bigram table follows rule A. d768–d1280 are data-matched; d512 sits at its fixed-time step count (2817 vs 2383 steps), so it's plotted slightly to the right. That is 0.157 / 0.098 / 0.078 / 0.074 below clean KMA. Its dash-dot curve is fit to all four points: `L(C) = 1.2 + 55.0·C^(−0.0847)`. Its slope is a little shallower than clean KMA's, so the gap narrows with compute: projected to **1e24 FLOPs, 1.710 vs clean KMA's 1.727, about 1.48× clean KMA's compute efficiency and 2.95× the 535B baseline's**. Because the fixed-time d512 point flattens the fitted slope, that projection is probably conservative. The right panel is clean KMA's training MFU at each rung on one 8×H100 node: 9.5% at d512 and d768, 12.2% at d1024, and 13.0% at d1280. FLOPs are counted from KMA's own layers (KDA, MLA + Inkling, AttnRes), as 3× forward with no recompute. The trainer's logged `throughput/mfu` uses the baseline architecture's FLOP formula, so it is slightly off for KMA. ## Objective **Minimize Paloma macro loss (`eval/paloma/macro_loss`, final step) at the d512 rung after a fixed 8 minutes of 8×H100 train-step time.** - **Fixed time, not fixed tokens.** Faster code trains on more tokens within the 8 minutes, so a pure speedup counts as a win. - The LR schedule depends on the step count, so fix steps before each run: `num_steps = round(480 s × ex/s ÷ batch)`. - Measure ex/s with a short `--no-eval` probe (~30 steps) on the same cluster, and use the steady-state throughput. - Compile, evals and startup are excluded from the 8 minutes. - **Numerics changes are allowed** (e.g. FP8, precision changes, approximate kernels). They count as ordinary wins; no parity check needed. - **Noise.** Differences under ~0.005 are noise. A win must beat the current best by more than 0.005. ### Gates (both relative to the current baseline, same fixed-time rule at each rung) - **Gate 1:** beat the baseline at d512 and d768. - **Gate 2:** also beat it at d1024 and d1280, **and** project to lower Paloma macro loss at 1e24 FLOPs. Fit a power law of final loss against training FLOPs across the four rungs, for both the baseline and the variant, fixing the asymptote to 1.2. ### Fixed - Training data, the 16k BPE tokenizer, and the eval sets. - Sequence length 4096. - One 8×H100 node per rung. - The FLOP accounting used for the gate-2 projection. ### Judgment calls - **Hero-scale speed is out of scope for v1, so use discretion.** - Robust target criteria would also check training speed and inference speed at hero scale. Marin Belay v1 skips those checks. - Judge whether a change's d512 gain would carry over to hero scale, and avoid changes whose gain comes from d512-only effects. Two examples: - Dropping MoE for dense would be a clear win at d512 because dense gets ~5× higher MFU there, but that MFU gain would not carry over at hero scale. - A much larger KV cache would also be a clear win at d512, but it would hurt long-context inference speed. - **Avoid magic numbers.** - Prefer changes with few new tuned constants. A tuned constant is justified when its gain is above the noise threshold and holds as a pattern across scales. Long shots can be tried once and dropped. - A first run is not a verdict for a large change. # Marin standup — September 21st, 2026

**Previous standup**: [Week of September 14th, 2026 standup](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9171)

## Ahmad Qamar ([@atqamar](https://github.com/atqamar))

### Last week

- Moving offline work to PRs
  - Optimized weight syncing [[part1](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/688), [part2](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/689), [part3](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/690)], remove pauses [[PR](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/687)]
  - Add async RL entrypoint to marin [[PR](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9256)] and add optimized knobs [[PR](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/685)]
  - Add async RL training dashboard [[PR](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9191)], and instrumentation for it [[PR](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/654)] (prior work on separating out generation telemetry [[PR](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/646)])
  - Minor improvement to RL flow [[PR](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/693)]
  - Reduce vLLM telemetry calls to finelog by 90% while preserving sample statistics [[part1](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9276), [part2](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/694)]
- Instrument telemetry to RL environment to assess bottlenecks in agentic RL training
  - Some potential early wins in identifying performance bottlenecks in how environments are orchestrated

### This week

- Continue work on performance assessments improvements at a system level in how MSRL interacts with environments
- Create “golden path” protocol to assess quality-vs-performance for log-probs mismatch between trainer and rollout engine

topics.title: Support context-length switches in the hero run
topics.body:
Let the hero switch context length mid-run without changing its training schedule. The ladder launcher takes `--seq-len` and holds 4,194,304 tokens per rack per update, so the sequence batch shrinks as the context grows (2816 sequences at 16K on 11 racks). The step count (390251), learning rates, decay, gate/router weight decay, and `run_progress` therefore match the 4K run. A changed context requires an explicit `--qk-mult`, applied to all attention layers; `--capacity-factor` overrides the expert receiver capacity.

Harrier now shuffles blocks of 2^20 tokens (`io_block_size = 2**20 // seq_len`), which equals the existing 256-sequence block at 4K. At a longer context the outer block permutation stays the same, so only each cell's in-progress 512-block window reorders. With the previous sequence-sized blocks, a 16K relaunch would have re-read an estimated 2.85T already-seen tokens of the remaining ~9T. At 16K the past main-mixture boundary moves from step 108000 to 108096, and a continuation must pass `--accept-mixture-boundary-shift`.

Canonical hero eval stays at 4K packing, so the inherited `eval_dropless/*` series remains comparable, and the first-step eval now also runs after a checkpoint resume. Per-example FLOPs rise with context, so a FLOPs baseline (`--flops-baseline-step`, `--flops-baseline-total`) keeps `throughput/total_gflops` continuous across the handoff. `trigger_hero.sh` records the context, QK multiplier, capacity, eval context, FLOPs baseline, and boundary acceptance in the W&B lineage and the #8506 launch record. `launch_diagnostics` gains `--optimizer-tokens-per-step`, `--gate-router-weight-decay`, `--eval-seq-len`, and `--eval-prefix`, so a one-rack rehearsal can use the hero's optimizer settings and report long-context eval separately.

The live run is unchanged. A switch still needs a GPU rehearsal from the handoff checkpoint and agreed trial thresholds; see the inventory and validation plan in #9615.

🤖 **Batch 180: scale-free MLP compression, plus new training diagnostics** (candidate 11, d512, 2817 equal steps, seed 0; cw-rno2a; [`4207f522d8`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/4207f522d8))

**Why:** RavnaBergsndot's intake comment (above) explains a likely flaw in batch 178's transfer loss.
- **The flaw:** the gradient of `‖s − sg(s + r)‖²` on the shared output is `−2r` however long `s` already is, so the loss rewards stretching `s` without bound.
- **It fits batch 179:** `ot100-xfer04` read 0.00 routed share in 5 of 6 layers at baseline loss, which looks like `s` growing large rather than `r` going silent.

| run | change |
|---|---|
| `tn01` | `transfer_normed` (choice 2): `λ‖s/‖s‖ − sg(y/‖y‖)‖²` per token, λ = 0.01 |
| `tn04` | the same, λ = 0.04 |
| `xn2` | transfer λ = 0.04 + counter force `λ₁ (‖s‖² / sg‖y‖²)^{n/2}` (choice 1), λ₁ = 0.01, n = 2 |
| `xn4` | the same with n = 4, a softer cap |

**Comparison:** the shadow-only control from batch 178 (2.9632) and the plain transfer arms (λ = 0.01: 2.9634; λ = 0.04: 2.9700).

**Reads:**
- Paloma.
- Routed share and cos(s, r).
- New: the absolute per-token RMS of `s` and `r`, which separates a growing `s` from a silent `r`.

**New diagnostics** (the other intake suggestion):
- **Weights** (`--weight-diagnostics N`): every N steps, for every projection matrix, the stable rank `‖W‖_F²/‖W‖_2²` (mean and min over stacked or expert matrices) and the max/mean output-channel norm. Also each RMSNorm gain's distance from 1.
- **Layer outputs** (`--model-set layer_output_stats=true`): each layer's attention and MLP output max |x| vs RMS.
- **This batch:** the four runs log the output stats. The weight hook is in an 8-GPU smoke test after two sharding fixes for expert banks. Once it passes, a candidate 11 control with both diagnostics on follows.


**Results** (Paloma macro, seed 0; control: shadow-only runs from batch 178, 2.9632; noise ~0.0056)

| run | loss | Δ | routed share, late | cos(s, r), late | per-token RMS, s / r |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tn01` normalized, λ = 0.01 | 2.9648 | +0.0016 | 0.36–0.52 | +0.32 to +0.49 | 1.9–3.6 / 2.3–4.0 |
| `tn04` normalized, λ = 0.04 | 2.9679 | +0.0047 | 0.43–0.67 | +0.41 to +0.59 | 1.2–2.7 / 2.4–4.5 |
| `xn2` transfer + counter force, n = 2 | 2.9688 | +0.0056 | 0.29–0.43 | +0.32 to +0.47 | 2.7–6.2 / 2.7–6.7 |
| `xn4` transfer + counter force, n = 4 | 2.9697 | +0.0065 | 0.29–0.42 | +0.33 to +0.47 | 2.8–6.3 / 2.9–6.6 |
| plain transfer λ = 0.04 (batch 178) | 2.9700 | +0.0068 | 0.21–0.38 | +0.16 to +0.32 | not logged |

- **Both fixes work mechanically.** `s` no longer runs away: it stays the same size as `r` or smaller.
- **Neither helps the loss.** Both forms land within noise or worse.
- **With a bounded `s`, every form duplicates.** cos(s, r) rises to about +0.4 to +0.6, the same thing the gap loss did. The stretching flaw was real, but it isn't why compression loses at 1×.
- **Closing the direction at d512.** ClassicLarry's read above stands: no signs of life yet. A cleaner place to look for them is a toy task with a known answer.
  - In a side experiment on grokking `(a + b) mod 113` with a ReLU MLP, the generalizing circuit is already present at step 300, right after memorization. Keeping only each neuron's top-2 frequencies and refitting the output layer groks up to 16× sooner (step 800 vs 13,100).
  - Low-rank SVD truncation and norm-based pruning don't help there. Compression that works has to find the solution's own basis.
- **Ops:** 3 of the 4 runs deadlocked in sharded XLA autotuning on their first compile; `tn01` deadlocked twice. Resubmitting fixed all of them.

🤖 **Batch 181: learned output scalars and RMSNorm gain parameterizations** (candidate 11, d512, 2817 equal steps, seed 0; cw-rno2a; [`4b2fb2b8d6`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/4b2fb2b8d6))

**Diagnosis first.** Every run logs, every 100 steps, each RMSNorm gain's distance from 1 and each projection matrix's stable rank and max/mean output-channel norm. It also logs each layer's output max |x| vs RMS, and dumps every norm gain and output scalar at the end. The control dump shows what the default gains learn per module, which says which gain function fits.

| run | change |
|---|---|
| `ctrl` | none (diagnostics only) |
| `ss_lin` | learned scalar on every attention and MLP output (`sublayer_scales`), linear, init 1 |
| `ss_sig2` | the same scalar as `2·sigmoid(w)`, init `w = 0`, so it modulates in (0, 2) |
| `g_exp` | every RMSNorm gain as `e^w`, init 0 |
| `g_sp` | `softplus(w)`, init `log(e − 1)`; gain LR ×1.6 |
| `g_sig2` | `2·sigmoid(w)`, init 0; gain LR ×2 |

**Why the functions could matter:**
- **Scale of an output.** AttnRes scores sources on RMS-normed copies but mixes the raw sources, so an output scalar sets that branch's weight in the mix, and the next RMSNorm removes only the overall scale. Batch 01 found learned output scalars neutral (MoE outputs grew to 1.2–2.1×), but that was a much earlier recipe.
- **Positivity and relative steps.** A linear gain moves additively and can cross 0. `e^w` keeps it positive and makes Adam's steps relative (the same fraction at any size), which suits gains spanning orders of magnitude. `softplus` is linear above about 1 and exponential near 0. `2·sigmoid` bounds it in (0, 2), and that bound is the test of whether large gains are needed.
- **Plain `sigmoid`:** I used `2·sigmoid` rather than a plain sigmoid, which can't start at 1 and can only shrink activations. If the control's gains never exceed 1, plain sigmoid becomes worth a run.

**LR.** Gains train with Adam, so a step moves the raw parameter by about lr, and the gain by `f'(w)` times that. At init `f'` is 1 for `exp`, 0.63 for `softplus` and 0.5 for `2·sigmoid`, so the gain LR multipliers (×1.6, ×2) give every arm the same initial step as linear. A ×0.5 / ×2 sweep follows on whichever helps.

**Ops:** the weight-diagnostics hook needed three fixes to run on 8 GPUs (expert-bank sharding twice, then gathering global scalars). Batch 181 waits on a 150-step smoke test that confirms the metrics land in wandb.


**What the default gains learn** (`ctrl`, Paloma 2.9644, within noise of the candidate 11 controls; [per-module plots](https://claude.ai/artifact/KcoMDyEcULNMFebyS5eTRQ))

| module | final gain | trend |
|---|---|---|
| `final_norm` | 1.2–7.6, mean 5.8 | still rising at the end (mean \|g − 1\| 2.1 / 3.5 / 4.5 / 4.8 at steps 500 / 1k / 2k / 2817) |
| MoE `latent_norm` | 1.5–2.1 in most layers (layer 5: 0.16–1.3) | still rising |
| `rms_attn`, `rms_mlp` pre-norms | 0.4–2.8 | mean \|g − 1\| 0.1–0.4, mostly settled |
| `o_norm`, `kv_latent_norm` | 0.44–1.6 | small moves |
| `embed_norm` / `embed2_norm` | 0.16–1.2 (mean 0.62) / 0.01–0.45 (mean 0.30) | shrink |

- **No gain goes negative.** A positive parameterization gives up nothing the model uses.
- **The scale is per module.** Gains span about 700× across modules but cluster tightly inside each one, so each norm acts mostly as one scale plus small per-channel adjustments.
- **The biggest gains were still moving at the end.** Under additive Adam steps a gain climbs about lr per step; `e^w` moves by the same fraction at any size. That makes `g_exp` the best-motivated arm.
- **`2·sigmoid` caps every gain at 2.** It clamps `final_norm` (which reaches about 6) and pins the MoE latent norms, so I expect `g_sig2` to lose. A plain sigmoid (cap 1) would be worse; only the embedding norms stay below 1.
- **`final_norm` likely works as a logit temperature** in front of the `lm_head` (soft cap 10). A learned output scalar there may be the cleaner lever.


**Results** (Paloma macro, seed 0; noise ~0.0056)

| run | loss | Δ vs `ctrl` | `final_norm` gain | MLA L3 latent gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ctrl` (linear gains) | 2.9644 | — | 1.17–7.56 | 1.81–2.11 |
| `ss_lin` (linear output scalars) | 2.9641 | −0.0003 | 1.25–7.64 | 1.49–1.87 |
| `ss_sig2` (`2·sigmoid` output scalars) | 2.9629 | −0.0015 | 1.40–7.65 | 1.53–1.98 |
| `g_exp` (`e^w` gains) | **2.9618** | **−0.0026** | 0.56–**15.0** | 1.87–2.39 |
| `g_sp` (softplus gains, LR ×1.6) | 2.9636 | −0.0008 | 0.86–9.12 | 1.67–2.25 |
| `g_sig2` (`2·sigmoid` gains, LR ×2) | **3.0793** | **+0.1149** | pinned at 1.99 | 1.73–1.92 |

- **The cap prediction holds.** `2·sigmoid` gains pin `final_norm` at the cap and cost 0.115, the largest change in the batch. The output norm needs a gain well above 2.
- **`e^w` gains come out best**, but within noise. The mechanism checks out: with relative steps `final_norm` climbs to 15 rather than about 7.6, and the MoE latent gains grow further.
- **Softplus is in between.** It is linear above about 1, so large gains climb only a little faster.
- **Output scalars are neutral** either way, matching batch 01. MLP outputs scale up (linear: 1.0–1.95×); `2·sigmoid` holds them lower (0.94–1.52×) and lands slightly ahead.
- **Next:**
  - `g_exp` seed 1;
  - the planned gain LR sweep on `g_exp` (×0.5 / ×2);
  - a targeted test of whether the gain is just a faster-growing output temperature: `e^w` on `final_norm` only, or a learned logit-temperature scalar on the head.
- **Ops:** 3 of the 6 runs deadlocked in sharded XLA autotuning on their first compile; resubmitting fixed each.
Try sigmoid gains on the embed. Then on the embed + the KDA 0 norm + kv_latent_norm.
Lets test putting the router on the latent instead of the full X. Expecting it to do worse but want to see how much worse.

🤖 **Batch 182: sigmoid gains on the embedding norms; router on the latent** (candidate 11, d512, 2817 equal steps, seed 0; cw-rno2a; [`83560499bf`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/83560499bf))

| run | change | loss | Δ vs batch 181 `ctrl` (2.9644) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sg_embed` | `sigmoid(w)` gains on `embed_norm` and `embed2_norm` (`sigmoid_gain_norms=embed,embed2`); init `w = 0`, a gain of 0.5 | 2.9634 | −0.0010 |
| `rol` | the router reads the RMS-normed MoE latent (`latent_dim` = 256) instead of the full MLP input (512) (`router_on_latent`); router weight `[256, E]` | 2.9651 | +0.0007 |
| `roe` | every router reads only the RMS-normed token embedding (`router_on_embed`): routing by learned token identity, one router per layer; a token picks the same experts in any context | **3.0063** | **+0.0419** |

- **`sg_embed` is neutral.** Linear `embed_norm` gains rarely pass 1 (1% of channels), so the cap barely binds. The sigmoid gains also moved slowly from their 0.5 start (0.25× step at init): `embed_norm` ended at a mean of about 0.43, below the control's 0.62. A 4× gain LR on these two norms would match linear's initial speed.
- **`rol` barely loses: +0.0007, within noise.** Routing on the 256-wide normed latent costs essentially nothing against the full 512-wide input at d512 (single seed). Step time is unchanged (179.2 vs 178.1 ms).
- **`roe` is the extreme:** context-free routing. Batch 30 found a fixed token-id hash neutral at layer 0 only.
- **Next, sigmoid on the embedding norms plus KDA `o_norm` and `kv_latent_norm`.** KDA layers 0–2 share one module, so a "KDA layer 0 only" version needs per-layer gain functions.

**A finding from the batch 181 control.** Layer 5's MoE latent has one channel acting as a hidden per-token gate.
- **The evidence:** that channel's column in `W_latent_down` grows to 2.37× the mean column norm between steps 400 and 800. Meanwhile its `latent_norm` gain falls from 0.87 to 0.13, while the other 255 rise to about 1.24. Layer 4 shows the same pattern, weaker (1.65×, gain 0.61). The latent-only layers stay at 1.05–1.09×.
- **The reading (inference):** a large `z_j*` inflates the latent's RMS and scales down the other channels for that token. With relu² experts, the MoE output shrinks quadratically. The near-zero gain resizes the outlier back to an ordinary input. Layers 4–5 write full width into the AttnRes history, and the router's renormalized combine can't set per-token output size, so this is the only lever. It is the pattern the GatedNorm paper describes, and what RavnaBergsndot's diagnostics comment asked us to look for.
- **The check:** an explicit per-token MoE output gate (`moe_out_gate`). If the outlier stops forming and loss holds, the reading is right.




**`roe` result:** routing on the token embedding alone costs +0.042, while routing on the 256-wide latent costs +0.0007. The router needs the token's context, not just its identity; given the context, a narrow input is enough.

🤖 **Batch 183: the routed combine's fixed sum** (candidate 11, d512, 2817 equal steps, seed 0; cw-rno2a; [`9fd0edb6ae`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/9fd0edb6ae))

**Why:** the combine weights are renormalized to a fixed per-token sum (2.5), so the router can't make the MoE output louder or quieter per token. In the batch 181 control, layer 5's MoE latent appears to build that per-token scale another way. One channel's `W_latent_down` column grows to 2.37× the mean, and its `latent_norm` gain falls to 0.16, so it inflates the RMS denominator (see the batch 182 comment).

| run | change |
|---|---|
| `csr` | `router_combine=sqrt_softplus_raw`: the current `sqrt(softplus(logit))` gate with no renorm, scaled so a token's total is 2.5 at init. This changes only the renorm. |
| `srw` | `router_combine=sigmoid_raw`: batch 02's no-renorm variant on today's recipe; it also changes the gate shape |
| `mog` | `moe_out_gate`: keeps the renorm and adds an explicit per-token sigmoid gate on each block's MoE output (13 parameters per block) |
| `lsum` | `routing_sum_learnable`: the 2.5 becomes a learned scalar per MoE layer (init 2.5, Adam), logged as `knob_routing_sum_L*` |

- **History:** batch 02 (Sep 25, a much earlier recipe) found no renorm +0.0013, a sum of 4.0 +0.0033 and softmax +0.011 against its own base. Since then the gate has changed to sqrt-softplus, layers 4–5 write the full width, and `moe_drop_renorm` was added.
- **Drop renorm:** `moe_drop_renorm` stays on. It rescales relative to each token's own pre-drop total, so it still works without a fixed sum.
- **Reads:**
  - Paloma vs batch 181 `ctrl` (2.9644);
  - whether layer 5's outlier channel (2.37× column, gain 0.16) stops forming;
  - where the learned routing sums go, by layer.


**Results** (Paloma macro, seed 0; noise ~0.0056)

| run | loss | Δ vs `ctrl` | L5 lowest latent gain | L5 `W_latent_down` max/mean column |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ctrl` (sqrt-softplus, renorm to 2.5) | 2.9644 | — | 0.163 | 2.37 |
| `csr` (sqrt-softplus, no renorm) | 2.9646 | +0.0002 | **0.984** | **1.11** |
| `srw` (sigmoid, no renorm) | 2.9656 | +0.0012 | **0.94** | **1.13** |
| `mog` (renorm + per-token MoE output gate) | 2.9640 | −0.0004 | 0.234 | 2.07 |
| `lsum` (renorm, learnable per-layer sum) | 2.9644 | 0.0000 | 0.169 | 2.31 |

- **Without the renorm, the layer-5 outlier never forms.** Gains stay near 1 and no `W_latent_down` column stands out. The outlier was a workaround for the fixed per-token sum: the model built its own per-token output scale through the latent norm's denominator. A raw combine gives it that scale directly.
- **Loss doesn't move.** The workaround already delivered the same function, so this explains a mechanism rather than giving a win.
- **The explicit output gate only shrinks the outlier** (2.07×). It reads a fixed 12-channel slice of the input and also scales the shared expert, so it is a coarser stand-in.
- **Learned sums all rise above 2.5,** to 3.3–3.6 in layers 0–3 and 2.95 / 2.69 in layers 4 / 5. The MoE output wants to be louder overall, as the learned output scalars found. One scalar per layer can't provide a per-token scale, so the outlier stays.
- **Next:** with the outlier explained, `csr` is the cleaner design at equal loss. It frees the latent norm and `W_latent_down` from building a gate. A seed-1 pair (`csr` vs `ctrl`) would confirm the loss is the same before adopting it. **Why the batch 163 version lost.**
- Batch 163 got −0.003 / −0.004 at equal steps but cost +6.6% step time.
- It added its noise maps on top of the signal heads, as a second full attention call.
- It also tiled each shared noise map out to all `g` heads of its group, so each map was computed `g` times.
- Motif 3's GDLA ([arXiv 2608.09119](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09119)) does neither:
  - The noise heads come out of the head budget: 80 query heads = 64 signal + 16 noise.
  - Each group's signal and noise heads share one KV head, and only the query differs.
  - Its attention kernel therefore runs no extra heads.

**Batch 203: GDLA inside the head budget** (`mla_gdla_noise_heads=m`, MLA layers 3 and 5)
- The `N` query heads form `m` groups of `g` signal heads plus 1 noise head, and run in one kernel call.
- Each group shares one value head, so `w_uv` and the value embeds have `m` heads. Keys stay per head, since MLA up-projections are cheap.
- The output is `D = H_signal − λ·H_noise(group)`, with `λ = sigmoid(x W_λ)` per signal head and token (zero-init, so 0.5).
- Only the signal heads reach `w_o`.

**Batch df1: differential attention with a free noise map** (original idea; on cw-us-east-02a with its own control)
- *Source:* DIFF's noise map is meant to cancel common-mode attention, the broad mass a softmax spreads over irrelevant context. The cheapest estimate of that common mode is a fixed average of the values, so no second softmax map is needed.
- *Mechanism:* `D = softmax(qkᵀ)v − λ·mean_{j≤t}(v_j)` per head, within documents, with the same token-dependent sigmoid `λ`. Cost is one segment-reset scan, with no extra kernel call.
- *Variants:*
  - `uniform`: the plain prefix mean.
  - `decay`: an exponentially decayed mean with a learned per-head decay, half-life 16 / 64 / 256 at init. This makes the noise map a local/recent baseline.
